n1.text: Week 1. The design pod looks like a bookshop exploded inside a greenhouse. Kai is pinning colour swatches to a board, humming.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: Fresh blood! Settle an argument for me. Lighthouse launch screen: calm ocean blue, or 'the future is now' electric violet?

choices.text: 'Violet. Make them feel something.'
'Blue. People trust blue.'
'Why not the green from your plant there? It's lovely.'

violet.speaker: Kai
violet.text: YES. Finally, someone with a pulse. Marcus said violet was 'a lot.' Marcus thinks beige is 'a lot.'

blue.speaker: Kai
blue.text: Ugh, sensible. Correct, probably. I'll make the blue sing, just for you.

green.speaker: Kai
green.text: ...Oh. Oh, that's actually perfect. That's alive. You just did my job better than me in four seconds. Rude. I love it.

end.speaker: Kai
end.text: Come back any time. The pod has snacks and zero deadlines we respect.

n1.text: Week 2. You're eating a sad sandwich over your keyboard when a shadow falls across your desk.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: Absolutely not. Lunch is not a keyboard activity. Come on. Café. Real food. Laptops stay here, they'll survive without us.

choices.text: Close the laptop and go.
'I have a deadline at two.'

go.text: Down in the café, Kai orders for both of you without asking, and is right about everything.

n5.speaker: Kai
n5.text: See? You look human again. People forget that the work gets better when you leave it alone for an hour.

deadline.speaker: Kai
deadline.text: There's always a deadline at two. There'll be one at two tomorrow, and the day after. I'll bring you a muffin. That's my compromise.

n7.text: Twenty minutes later, a muffin appears beside your keyboard, with a tiny drawing of you on the napkin, scowling at a spreadsheet.

end.text: You catch yourself smiling at nothing in particular for the rest of the afternoon.

kl_more_1.text: Back at your desk, a sticky note appears on your monitor in Kai's handwriting: 'Lunch is a human right. This is your one warning. Next time I bring a whistle.'

choices.text: Write back: 'Tomorrow. 12:30. Bring the whistle anyway.'
Stick it to your notebook and keep it.

n1.text: Week 3. Lunch on the rooftop. Kai is sketching the skyline and, you slowly realise, also you.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: Don't move. You've got a very good 'thinking about something you shouldn't be' face. It's very drawable.

choices.text: Hold still and let them finish.
Lean over to see the sketchbook.
'What are you thinking about, when you draw?'

still.text: Ten minutes. You don't move. Kai tears the page out and hands it to you. It's really, really good.

peek.speaker: Kai
peek.text: Hey! Unfinished work is private. ...Fine. It's you, looking out at the city like you're trying to decide whether to jump into it.

think.speaker: Kai
think.text: Honestly? That I'm happy. It's a weird thing to notice. I didn't used to be. Drawing is how I check.

end.text: The sketch ends up pinned to your monitor. People ask who drew it. You find you like saying their name.

n1.text: Week 4. After the all-hands. Marcus announces mandatory weekend work until launch. The floor groans. Kai doesn't groan. Kai stands up.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: I'll do my hours, and I'll do them brilliantly. But I'm not working weekends. Not again. I'll put it in writing if you'd like.

n3.text: Later, in the pod, Kai is shaking slightly and pretending not to be.

choices.text: 'That took guts. Why does it matter so much to you?'
'You might have just made yourself a target.'
'I'm going to work the weekends. I need this launch.'

why.speaker: Kai
why.text: Because the last place I worked, I said yes to every weekend for two years. Then one Tuesday I couldn't get out of bed. I'm not going back there. Not for any launch.

target.speaker: Kai
target.text: Maybe. Probably. Better a target than a ghost. I've been a ghost, it's worse.

honest.speaker: Kai
honest.text: ...Okay. That's honest, and I respect honest. Just promise me you'll notice if it starts costing more than it's paying.

end.text: On your way home you realise Kai is the only person on the floor who looked relieved after the meeting. Everyone else just looked tired.

n1.text: Week 5. You've had four hours of sleep. Your eyes feel like they've been sandpapered. Kai puts a hand flat on your keyboard.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: Okay. Intervention. Afternoon off. Rooftop, me, a terrible paperback and a flask of tea. Marcus will survive.

choices.text: Take the afternoon off with Kai.
'An hour. I can give you an hour.'
'Kai, I can't. Not this week.'

off.text: You nap on a rooftop bench with your head on a rolled-up jacket while Kai reads aloud from the worst detective novel ever written. It is the best afternoon of the quarter.

hour.speaker: Kai
hour.text: An hour I can work with. Phone in my bag. No, the whole phone. Thank you.

no.speaker: Kai
no.text: Not this week. It's never this week. ...Okay. I'll stop pushing. But the offer doesn't expire.

end.text: Kai doesn't say 'I told you so' later. They just quietly leave a bottle of water on your desk every morning that week.

n1.text: Week 6. Friday, 6pm. Kai leans over the partition with a flyer for a Saturday flea market.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: Vintage lamps, terrible jewellery, dumplings the size of your fist. I go every month. Come with me. Bring nothing but appetite.

choices.text: 'I'm in. I'll even leave my laptop at home.'
'I've got launch prep. Rain check?'

yes.text: Saturday. Kai haggles for a hideous ceramic frog with total conviction and gives it to you. You eat dumplings on a kerb. Nobody mentions Lighthouse once.

n5.speaker: Kai
n5.text: This. This is what I mean. Life is supposed to have a weekend in it. ...Thanks for coming. Really.

no.speaker: Kai
no.text: Rain check. Sure. My rain checks expire, by the way. Very quietly. Just so you know.

end.text: Monday morning, there's a tiny drawing of a ceramic frog on a sticky note on your screen.

n1.text: Week 7. Late. Kai is still at the office, which is so unusual that you stop.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: Don't look at me like that. I'm leaving in five minutes. I just... got an email from my old agency. They want me back. Double the money.

n3.speaker: Kai
n3.text: It would be the same thing again. The weekends. The 2am calls. The bit where I stop drawing for fun. But it's double the money.

choices.text: 'You already know the answer. You told it to me in week four.'
'Double is a lot. Maybe it'd be different this time.'
'Whatever you choose, I'll still be here.'

know.speaker: Kai
know.text: ...Yeah. I did. I just wanted someone to say it back to me in my own words. Thanks. Delete. Done.

money.speaker: Kai
money.text: Maybe. People always think it'll be different. ...I'm going to sleep on it.

here.speaker: Kai
here.text: That's... a very good reason not to go somewhere else, actually. Huh.

end.text: They switch the lamp off, and for once they leave before you do.

kw_more_1.text: On the way to the lift, Kai stops at the window. The city is doing its usual night-time showing off.

kw_more_2.speaker: Kai
kw_more_2.text: Here's the thing nobody tells you about being good at a job you hate. People keep offering you more of it. Double the money is just double the thing that made you stop drawing on the train.

choices.text: 'Then don't sell them the train.'
'What do you draw on the train now?'

kw_more_4.speaker: Kai
kw_more_4.text: Commuters. Pigeons. The back of your head, once, when you fell asleep on the way to the client site. It's a very good head. Don't let it go to it.

n1.text: Week 8. The launch visuals are late. Marcus wants them tonight. Kai has already left, on time, as promised.

n2.speaker: Marcus
n2.text: I need those files by morning. Can you reach Kai, or do I need to escalate?

choices.text: 'I'll finish what I can myself. Leave Kai out of it tonight.'
Call Kai and ask them to come back in.
'Give us until noon. They'll be better for it.'

cover.text: You stay until midnight wrestling with layer masks. Your version is functional. Kai's version, at 9am, is art. They see your file and go very quiet.

n5.speaker: Kai
n5.text: You did this for me? Badly — sorry, but badly. You did it badly for me. Nobody's ever done anything badly for me before.

call.speaker: Kai
call.text: ...Right. Of course. I'm coming in. It's fine. It's fine. It's fine.

n7.text: It is not fine. You can hear it in the way they say it three times.

noon.speaker: Marcus
noon.text: Noon. Not a minute later. ...You're getting good at this, you know. Protecting people.

end.text: The files arrive at 11:52, and they are gorgeous.

kd_more_1.speaker: Kai
kd_more_1.text: Next time something's on fire at six, call me. Not to come in. Just to tell me it's on fire. I'd rather know than find out you stayed until midnight on my account.

choices.text: 'Deal. Fires get reported. Weekends stay yours.'
'You'd come in anyway. I know you.'

kd_more_3.speaker: Kai
kd_more_3.text: ...Maybe. For you, I might. Don't tell anyone. It ruins my whole brand.

n1.text: Week 10. Kai finds you at the café with a printed email and a face that can't decide what it's doing.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: A studio across the sea wants me. Four-day week. Design lead. They saw the Lighthouse visuals. It's the dream. It's also very, very far from here.

choices.text: 'Go. And let me visit on all your Fridays off.'
'Stay. Make this place better instead. With me.'
'That's amazing. You should take it.'

go.speaker: Kai
go.text: ...You'd visit. On Fridays. You'd take Fridays off to visit me. Who even are you now? I'm so proud of you, it's unbearable.

stay.speaker: Kai
stay.text: With you. Okay. That's... a bigger reason than a four-day week, possibly. Let me sit with it.

polite.speaker: Kai
polite.text: Yeah. Yeah, I should. Thanks. ...I kind of hoped you'd say something else. Ignore me.

end.text: Kai folds the email into a tiny paper frog and puts it in your pocket.

cb_frog_1.speaker: Kai
cb_frog_1.text: The frog says hi, by the way. He lives on my windowsill now. He would absolutely hate the move.

n1.text: Week 11. Launch week. Kai's violet-and-plant-green launch screen goes up in the lobby. People stop to take photos of it.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: They're photographing my colours. My actual colours. ...Gala's next week. Are you going to look at me like that at the gala? Because I'll need to prepare.

choices.text: 'I'm going to look at you exactly like this.'
'Like what?' (You know exactly like what.)

coy.speaker: Kai
coy.text: Like the plant-green. Alive. Don't pretend. I've drawn your face too many times to fall for it.

kb_pre_1.text: Week 11. Launch week. Kai has stopped pretending to be calm and started reorganising the design pod's pens by colour, then by length, then by vibe.

kb_pre_2.speaker: Kai
kb_pre_2.text: Don't look at me. I'm fine. I'm a professional. I've only redone the loading animation nine times, which is a normal number of times.

choices.text: Take the mouse out of their hand. 'Nine is plenty.'
'Show me the ninth one.'

kb_pre_4.text: The ninth one is beautiful. So were the other eight. You tell them so, and for a second Kai looks like someone who has never heard that sentence in a workplace before.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Kai's launch screen glows violet and green behind the stage. At exactly 10pm, they find you and hold out a hand.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: It's ten. We said we'd leave at ten, remember? Real life. Dumplings. The frog misses you.

n3.text: You leave a work party early, on purpose, laughing, hand in hand. Behind you the gala goes on perfectly well without you.

n4.text: Months later there's a four-day week, a flat with too many plants, and a sketchbook full of you.

n5.text: ♥ ROMANCE ENDING: 'Log Off.' You chose a life with a weekend in it, and someone to share it with. Thanks for playing Kai's route.

cb_fridge_1.speaker: Kai
cb_fridge_1.text: You know the napkin drawing? My mum has it on her fridge now. I sent her a photo of yours. She said, and I quote, 'So this is the person.' I didn't correct her.

kt_more_1.text: Outside, the air is cool and the street is loud and nobody knows or cares that a launch just happened upstairs.

kt_more_2.speaker: Kai
kt_more_2.text: Do you know what I'm going to do tomorrow? Absolutely nothing. I'm going to do nothing so well they'll put it in a museum. And you're invited.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Kai dances with everyone, and with you twice. But at ten they leave, and you stay for the after-party with the directors.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: You're brilliant, you know. I just can't be the person waiting for you to log off. Call me when you're ready. I mean it. I'll pick up.

n3.text: ♡ BITTERSWEET ENDING: 'Call Me When You Log Off.' The feeling was real. The timing wasn't. Thanks for playing Kai's route.

cb_postcard_1.text: Three weeks later, a postcard arrives from across the sea. On the back, a tiny drawing of a frog in a very small suitcase. No words. You understand it perfectly.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Kai drags you onto the dance floor and declares you their 'official work best friend' to the entire design team.

n2.text: It's not a love story. It's something sturdy and warm and full of muffins with tiny drawings on the napkins.

n3.text: ◆ FRIENDSHIP ENDING: 'Official Work Best Friend.' Thanks for playing Kai's route.

kf_more_1.speaker: Kai
kf_more_1.text: For the record, if you ever need someone to tell you your slides are ugly and your shoes are perfect, I'm always available. Weekdays only. Until six.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Kai's colours fill the room. You realise you've barely spoken to them in weeks.

n2.text: They wave from across the room, friendly and far away. The rain checks expired quietly, just like they said.

n3.text: ○ ENDING: 'Rain Check.' Thanks for playing Kai's route.

km_more_1.text: Later, you find a drawing of the rooftop bench pinned to the design pod wall. Only one figure on it now, reading alone.

n1.speaker: Kai
n1.text: Deep in the colour zone right now. Come back with snacks and a strong opinion about fonts.

n1.speaker: Kai
n1.text: Saturday market? The frog wants a friend. A matching frog. Don't argue.
Week 8. Lunch at the café. Kai's phone buzzes for the third time. They stare at the screen as if it might bite.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: My mum. She calls every Thursday to ask whether I've 'got a proper job yet.' I'm leading design on a launch the CFO is personally watching. Apparently that's still 'drawing.'

choices.text: 'Answer it. On speaker. I'll back you up.'
'You don't have to pick up today.'
'Maybe she just worries about you.'

speaker.text: Kai answers. Their mum's voice fills the café: warm, sharp and entirely unconvinced. You lean in. 'Hi. I work with Kai. Their launch screen goes up in the lobby next week. People are already taking photos of it.'

n5.text: There is a long pause on the line. Then: 'Photos? Send me one.'

n6.speaker: Kai
n6.text: She asked for a photo. She has never once in my life asked for a photo. You absolute menace. Thank you.

skip.speaker: Kai
skip.text: ...Huh. Nobody's ever said that to me. I always pick up, and then I spend the afternoon feeling like a hobby.

n8.speaker: Kai
n8.text: I'll call her tonight. On my terms. With a photo of the launch screen. That'll confuse her for a week.

worry.speaker: Kai
worry.text: She does. That's the annoying part. She worries like people worry about the weather: constantly, and with no plan. ...Fine. I'll send her the photo. Happy?

mid.text: For the rest of lunch, Kai draws on a napkin: a tiny lobby, a tiny launch screen, and a tiny you standing in front of it.

n11.speaker: Kai
n11.text: Can I tell you something embarrassing? The no-weekends thing isn't only about burning out. Every weekend I worked at the old place, I was trying to prove her wrong. It never worked. You can't overtime your way into someone's approval.

choices.text: 'You don't have to prove anything to me.'
'So what would you do with a weekend that was really yours?'

e1.speaker: Kai
e1.text: ...Careful. Say things like that and I might start believing them.

e2.speaker: Kai
e2.text: Sleep in. The market. Draw something nobody's paying for. And, honestly? Spend it with someone who doesn't ask what I've achieved by Sunday.

n15.text: They don't look at you when they say it. They don't need to.

end.text: Kai folds the napkin and tucks it into your shirt pocket. 'For the fridge,' they say. 'Everyone needs one drawing on the fridge.'

n1.text: Week 9. A tiny gallery above a bike shop. Kai has six drawings on the wall, a bowl of crisps and the expression of someone awaiting sentencing.

n2.speaker: Kai
n2.text: It's not a real show. It's a 'community wall.' Nobody's coming. Which is fine. Which is ideal, actually.

n3.text: Twelve people come. One of them is a woman from a big design studio across the sea, and she looks at the drawings for a very long time.

choices.text: 'Go and talk to her. I'll guard the crisps.'
'Stay here with me. Let the work do the talking.'
Look closer at the drawings yourself.

brave.text: Kai goes. You watch them talk with their hands, the way they do when they forget to be nervous. When they come back, there's a business card in their fist.

n6.speaker: Kai
n6.text: She wants to 'have a conversation.' People like her don't have conversations. They make offers. ...Oh no.

stay.speaker: Kai
stay.text: The work talks. Right. The work is very quiet and I'm going to be sick.

n8.text: Ten minutes later the woman comes to them. There's a business card. Kai holds it as if it might go off.

look.text: Third drawing from the left: the rooftop. Two figures on a bench. One asleep on a rolled-up jacket, one reading a terrible detective novel.

lk1.speaker: Kai
lk1.text: ...I didn't think you'd notice. Everyone else thinks it's 'a study in light.' It's a study in the best afternoon of my quarter.

lk2.speaker: Kai
lk2.text: It's from the day you didn't come up for a break. I drew the person I wished had been there. Then I drew them as you anyway.

card.text: Behind you, the woman from the studio slips Kai a business card on her way out.

mid.speaker: Kai
mid.text: If they offer me something, it'll be far from here. You know that, right? You'd tell me to go. You're annoyingly good at telling people to go and be brave.

choices.text: 'I'd tell you to go. And I'd mean it.'
'I'd tell you to go. Then I'd miss you terribly.'
'Let's not talk about leaving tonight. It's your show.'

go.speaker: Kai
go.text: You would. That's the most infuriating thing about you, and the best.

miss.speaker: Kai
miss.text: ...Terribly. Okay. I'm putting that on the wall too. Metaphorically. Possibly literally.

tonight.speaker: Kai
tonight.text: My show. Yes. Six drawings and a bowl of crisps. Officially the most successful night of my life.

end.text: You walk Kai home past shuttered shops, the business card a small white weight in their pocket. Neither of you mentions it. Both of you think about it all the way.
